title: World War I Tracker Update — Mon Aug 10, 2026
summary: Private Roy Leslie Martin of Cobar, NSW, received a new named headstone at the CWGC's Fromelles (Pheasant Wood) Military Cemetery during commemorations marking the 110th anniversary of the Battle of Fromelles (19–20 July 1916), bringing the number of the 250 Pheasant Wood soldiers identified by name to 182. Martin's identity, confirmed via DNA analysis with the Fromelles Association of Australia, was first announced by the Australian Department of Defence in April 2026 alongside that of 2nd Lt. Duncan McKenzie. Separately, the July 9 burial of Canadian Private Albert Henry Detmold at Loos British Cemetery was updated with newly reported research establishing his Jewish heritage — his military attestation had listed him as Presbyterian, a discrepancy attributed to antisemitism documented among WWI-era Canadian recruits — and the graveside service's Jewish rite led by Rabbi Noteh Glogauer.

title: World War I Tracker Update — May 19, 2026
summary: Five new events added covering April–May 2026 WWI commemorations. On April 22, British soldier Private Reginald Blake (Essex Regiment) was buried at Loos British Cemetery Extension after DNA identification confirmed his identity 109 years after going missing near Lens in 1917. ANZAC Day on April 25 drew worldwide observances for the 111th anniversary of the Gallipoli landings, with dawn services at Anzac Cove and the Australian War Memorial broadcast live. On April 28, the Australian Department of Defence announced DNA identification of 2nd Lt. Duncan McKenzie (Passchendaele) and Pte. Roy Martin (Fromelles), bringing the total Fromelles identifications to 181 of 250. The 111th anniversary of the RMS Lusitania sinking (May 7, 1915) was marked by a ceremony at the Lusitania Memorial Garden at Old Head of Kinsale on May 7, while Cobh held its annual commemoration of the mass funeral of victims on May 10. A new claim was added on Italy's strategic decision to enter WWI in May 1915, and two new political profiles — General Aleksei Brusilov and Field Marshal Edmund Allenby — were added to the tracker.

title: World War I Tracker Update — Apr 19, 2026
summary: Four new events added for April 2026 covering WWI commemorations and historical discoveries. On April 1, descendants of the Choctaw Code Talkers gathered in Fort Worth, Texas, to unveil a historical marker honoring the WWI soldiers who pioneered Native American language code use. April 6 marked the 109th anniversary of the US declaration of war against Germany. On April 9, Canadian communities observed Vimy Ridge Day, and the Canadian War Museum acquired a century-old chair carved by a prisoner at the Spirit Lake WWI internment camp in Quebec. April 18 saw preparations underway across Australia and New Zealand for ANZAC Day 2026, marking the 111th anniversary of the Gallipoli landings.
